# 16 Give the class diagram its default theme

## Outcome

A class diagram rendered in a real browser is visible and legible: class frames, names,
annotations, compartment dividers, member text, all four relationship endpoint markers, dashed and
solid relationship lines, labels, multiplicity, namespace frames and notes all pick up the
existing `--siren-*` tokens, in both light and dark.

## Why this ticket exists

On the sequence board this was found only in the closing review: `theme/default.css` had no rules
for the new renderer's classes, so every stroke defaulted to `none` and every box filled black —
invisible in a browser while all tests passed, because jsdom never paints. `theme/default.test.ts`
now guards that, and this ticket extends the guard to the third diagram kind rather than
rediscovering the same defect.

**Rescheduled after round 2's review.** This ticket originally sat at the end of the board,
behind the animation ticket — which would have put the demo (ticket 06) on screen for several
rounds as black boxes and invisible lines, repeating the sequence board's mistake one ticket
later instead of avoiding it. It now runs immediately after the demo exists. The tickets that
land *after* this one and emit new classes (10, 14, 15) each own the theme files too and must
theme what they add; once this ticket's coverage test is in place it fails loudly if they don't,
which is the point.

One consequence of the round-2 renderer worth knowing before you start: the filled and hollow
diamonds share a single path shape and are told apart **only** by `siren-arrow-fill` versus
`siren-arrow-hollow`. Until this ticket lands, composition and aggregation are the same picture.
The same is true of the hollow triangle shared by inheritance and realization. These are not
cosmetic rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `theme/default.test.ts` gains a class-diagram block reusing its existing generic helpers
  (`renderThemedSVG`, `emittedSirenClasses`, `describeElement`) with a new every-feature class
  source — a rule must exist for every `siren-*` class the class renderer emits.
- [ ] Every drawn element in that diagram resolves a stroke or a fill, including elements carrying
  no class of their own (a class box's `rect` and its member `text` nodes).
- [ ] `siren-arrow-hollow` is filled with the surface color, not left transparent, so composition
  is visibly distinct from aggregation and inheritance from realization. Assert the two diamond
  markers resolve different fills — this is the one rule whose absence changes what the diagram
  *means*, not just how it looks.
- [ ] The class-diagram groups are added to the shared font-family rule alongside
  `.siren-participant`, `.siren-message`, `.siren-block`, `.siren-box` — otherwise member text
  renders in the browser default font while the layout sized the boxes with the theme's.
- [ ] Relationship lines keep the `stroke-dasharray` the renderer sets per relationship — the
  theme must not override a per-element dash.
- [ ] An author's inline `style` (ticket 14) still wins over the theme — asserted, since that is
  the whole premise of ADR-0008.
- [ ] Rules reference the existing color tokens directly rather than declaring new `:root` color
  tokens, for the cascade reason recorded in the sequence board's theme work (a new token declared
  at `:root` freezes its light value above any lower-scoped dark override).
- [ ] Verified by rasterizing a rendered class diagram with the stylesheet applied and looking at
  the image, in both light and dark. Say what you saw; do not claim a visual check you did not do.

## Test seam

`theme/default.test.ts`'s cascade-based coverage tests, plus manual rasterization.
